items.title: competing-start-cues
items.claim: Image 2 displays both a FIGHT button and STARTING IN 2, giving the player simultaneous manual-start and countdown cues.
items.reason: A newcomer may feel rushed before understanding the controls.
items.suggest: Make the introduction wait for FIGHT; reserve countdowns for transitions after the player has explicitly started.

items.title: result-combat-poses
items.claim: Image 18 announces ASMONGOLD WINS while Asmongold is shown kicking and HasanAbi remains in a standing guard pose.
items.reason: The fighter presentation does not reinforce the outcome as clearly as the headline does.
items.suggest: Use distinct winner-celebration and loser-defeat poses on the result screen, without changing the scored exchange.

items.title: empty-desktop-control-band
items.claim: Image 9 places the two sticks at opposite ends of a full-width dark band with an empty center beneath the arena.
items.reason: The desktop composition gives substantial visual space to an otherwise empty control area.
items.suggest: Use compact bottom-corner control panels on desktop and extend the arena into the released space, preserving the portrait-phone layout.

items.title: input-badges-lack-local-labels
items.claim: Image 6 identifies STANCE and TECHNIQUE in the top legend, but the individual move rows contain two input badges without those labels.
items.reason: Players must remember the legend's ordering while decoding each move.
items.suggest: Add labelled STANCE and TECHNIQUE columns within each technique group, keeping the input badges aligned beneath their respective labels.

items.title: front-kick-endpoint-unresolved
items.claim: In Image 13, the raised leg's endpoint does not show a clearly distinguishable bare-foot silhouette comparable to the planted foot, but the still cannot establish whether the foot is clipped or simply obscured by the pose.
items.reason: The striking limb needs a readable silhouette, but an unsupported anatomy correction could damage a valid sprite.
items.suggest: Inspect the unscaled source pose, atlas crop boundaries, and a short kick sequence before editing; expand the affected crop only if clipping is confirmed.
